title: How many ways can a square be cut into four equal areas?
description: A square is cut into four small squares, then into four long strips. Each small square then gets a dent on one edge and a bump of the same size on another edge, so the pieces change shape. The video stops on the question of how many ways there are to cut a square into four parts of equal area.
teaching_notes: One idea: parts can have equal area without having the same shape. Do not confirm any guess, because the lessons that follow settle what area is. Watch for children who think equal parts must look identical.

source: How many ways to cut a square into 4 equal areas?
video_script.why: Before any formula, the child meets the real question of what it means for two pieces to have the same area.
video_script.substitution: A square is divided into four parts of equal area in more than one way, and the cuts are then bent without changing any area.
video_script.anchor: the square that the book divides into four parts of equal area
maths_rules: The board is a square divided first into four equal small squares, then into four equal long strips.
In the third picture each small square has a dent pushed into one edge and an equal bump pushed out of another edge, so the four pieces keep equal area but change shape.
No numbers or lengths are drawn.
The open question: how many different ways are there to cut a square into four parts of equal area. The answer is never shown or hinted.
video_script.design: One idea: equal area does not need equal shape. The square stays on stage to the end. The open question is the last line before the think-and-tell.
